sections.body: Cyberbullying is repeated, deliberate online cruelty: mean messages, sharing embarrassing photos, excluding someone, or impersonation.
If it happens to you: don't reply in anger. Screenshot evidence, block, report on the platform, and tell a trusted adult.
If you see it: don't like or share. Privately check on the person ('Are you OK?') and report it. Bystanders can make a big difference.

quiz.q: Someone keeps sending you mean messages. What should you do?
options: Save evidence, block, report and tell an adult
hints: Replying in anger can make it worse.
Keeping proof helps adults and platforms act.
If someone keeps pushing you at school, you'd tell a teacher and explain what happened. Online is similar.
quiz.explain: Save evidence, block and report, and tell a trusted adult.

quiz.q: You see a cruel post about a classmate. What helps most?
options: Don't share it, check on them privately and report it
Like it so you fit in
hints: What would help the person being targeted?
If you saw someone pushed over in the playground, you'd help them up and tell a teacher.
quiz.explain: Don't spread it, support the person privately, and report it.
